Mark Plays Nuitai

A blind playtest of the pygame demo by Mark, an invented professional playtester, thinking out loud. His notes follow the episode.

Mark Hello again. We're back on the harbor dock in Kulāiwi, Kailo facing the Meialana, and nothing has been saved, because in two hours I still haven't found a save point. That's my first goal today: find one, or find out whether the game has one at all. After that I want to get north to the Great Boar, find the hunters' lodge to sell these Boar Hides, and get the poi sorted for Nene and the wake. Both of them are at full health, which is a nice change. Let's see what the harbor's got.

Mark Okay, field menu first: still no Save in there. Items, Element, Equip, Status, Party, Info, Config. So that's confirmed, the menu has nothing. The one odd item in my bag is "???" under Meals, and it reads "Makes whoever eats it sick." That's my banana experiment from last time. Good to know I kept evidence.

Mark Looking at the area map, the whole explored strip is tiny compared with all the black above it. The island goes much further north. I'm heading back east to the taro patch by the grocer, because last time I wanted taro for Nene's poi.

Mark Oh, I can just walk up to the patch and press z. "Picked 2 Taro." And then Hina says "Don't leave it bare. It should be replanted. I'll show you how." A choice: plant Taro or leave it bare. I replant. That's lovely, a tiny farming loop that teaches itself through a character instead of a tutorial box. I did the second plot too. I'll write down that taro grows back, "It takes a while to grow."

Mark North of the grocer is a path into Kulāiwi Forest. Two boars noticed me with the little exclamation marks before I could punch either one, so it's a two-on-two. Hina's in her light stance this time, which my notes say resists fire, so the fire boars shouldn't hurt her much.

Mark Turn order first, as always. Hina goes, I go, boars, and then it repeats. I'm opening each turn with Light, Medium, Strong, and the first Strong tends to be the one that gets dodged. Hina's strokes also fill her mana, five after one turn. Good, the mana bar is the hidden engine of this whole game. Everything good costs it.

Mark Something I did not know: the boars shift stance on their own. "Pua'a Hihiu A shifts to nature stance." And then B goes to fire. So I can't plan the whole fight from the first screen, which is good, I like that the enemy isn't a static sheet. Nature means weak to fire, so I use Sauté on A. "Weak!" pops up, 25, and the Burn icon shows.

Mark And here is the Combo, Tinju Surya, fire and sun together. It's grayed out. I tried it with Kailo then Hina side by side and still grayed, so I think it wants both of us at full mana, not just six. I've seen that before, I wrote it in my notes. The game never says why it's grayed out, which is a shame, because the name and the two little icons are such a good hook.

Mark Parry window on the last boar. Three blows: Light, Strong, Strong. I pressed each one at the time the narrator gave me and got "Parried!" three times. That feels great, and it even hurts the boar back, a 25 popped over it. Parrying is a real way to play, not a bonus.

Mark Won. The loot was "Noni Pulu, Boar Hide, Seer's Shell", and then the party sat down and ate and the HP climbed back to full. So the heal-after-a-win from Hina is doing something visible. Good. I'm going north.

Mark More boars. Three more fights in the orchard and the path north, and I can say what the pattern is now. The wild boar swaps stance on its own and digs a truffle to heal, then eats it: "+30". Kailo and Hina are both fire-resistant in their stances, so its fire kick shows "Resisted" and does 7 or 8. The first Strong blow still gets dodged more than the others. Drops so far: Boar Hide, a Flambé, Taro, and my stats ticked up: "PER up" for Kailo and "END up" for Hina. Use it and it grows, as the studio said.

Mark And now the Combo, finally. Both of us at seven out of seven, and Hina and Kailo back to back in the turn order. It opened a lights game: four buttons, a string that gets longer every round. The narrator tells me which light, I press it back: tab, tab, then tab tab z, then tab tab z x. It's Simon. Then a punch with a shrinking circle that I threw at twenty-six percent. 198 damage to a boar that normally takes forty a hit. That is a huge payoff. It is also the first time the game made me do a real task for a reward and it actually felt earned.

Mark What I like: the Combo costs full mana from both of us, side by side in the queue, so you build toward it. What I don't like: it grays out and never tells you the condition. I figured out "both at full" by trial and error. A single line, like "needs 7 mana each", would fix it.

Mark The orchard is a maze of bushes and palms and I spent a while bumping into walls trying to find the north gap I'd noted last time. I could not find a way in from the south. What I did find is a bridge on the east side that goes to a little island of banyan trees, with Papanoks, the roosters, standing around it. Banyans are Bandar's mark, according to the Loremaster, so someone planted these, or the order did. And there is a sandy road going north off the top of the island.

Mark Two roosters woke at once. One of them had a seven-blow Light string, a whole row of Y presses, 0.33 seconds apart. I parried the first six or so and took a little damage on the last. That is the cleanest parry rule yet: a string of identical blows is actually easier than a mixed one, because you can send the same key at an even rhythm. Kailo grew from 140 to 150 HP, "VIT up, END up, PER up". And the rooster dropped an Egg. Noelani's stew list needed Eggs. Good, one more ingredient.

Mark The bridge. A long wooden boardwalk heading north across the water, little islets with chests on either side, and a small man in a blue cap standing right in the middle of it. "Nuno sa Tulay says: Stop! Who goes there? This is MY bridge, nobody crosses... for free." Nuno sa Tulay is a Filipino folk figure, a goblin-ish dwarf that lives in a mound, and "sa tulay" means "on the bridge". Nice. A toll troll. "100 pule and you may cross." I have exactly zero pule. A choice: pay, or "I'm not paying that. This bridge is free for everyone to use.", or "I guess we'll have to find another way around."

Mark I'm Kailo. He's proud, he hates people taking things that are free, and he's got a pan. I stand my ground, I pick the second answer, and I own that choice. "No? NO? Then I'll take it out of your hide!" Boss music, "Boss Battle 1". I started this at 96 out of 150 HP from the roosters, which I now know was a mistake, but I'd have said I could not cover a hundred pule anyway.

Mark This fight is something. He has a new stance, spirit. He stirs a great cyclone that is Weak! for both of us, and "The lightning jumps to Kailo." He acts two or three times in a row because his time costs are tiny. My Combo did 95 and it said "Resisted". I could not heal: Hina's cure costs mana and I had none, and my Cook was grayed out because the Taro is in my pack, not in Kailo's battle bag. I never put a single item in the bags. That's on me, but it's also a game that does not tell you the bags matter. Escape is grayed out in a boss fight, no message why.

Mark "Hina falls." and then "Kailo falls." and then "The party has fallen." Game Over, a black screen with two words. And nothing saved, so I'm honestly afraid of what this does. Let me see.

Mark Back to the title screen. New Game, Continue grayed out, Options. And the corner says "save 21", which I read as a build number. So Game Over throws you out to the title with nothing to continue. That means every minute of this episode so far, the taro, the combo, the rooster egg, is gone, and the only way forward is New Game. I said last time that having no save point makes every risk too costly. I just paid for that sentence. I'm not angry at the troll; I'm a bit angry at a game that lets me walk into a boss at two thirds health with no warning, no save and no way to flee. A boss gate should at least say "boss".

Mark Fine. New Game. I know where things are now, so this should go faster, and I'm going to do three things differently: put Taro and a Noni Pulu in the battle bags, hunt for a place to save, and not touch that bridge until I have pule or a plan.

Mark So the tutorial fight again, from the top. I know what it says, which does help me appreciate how it's built. Hina interrupts the fight to teach: the faces on the right are who goes next, the yellow bars are stamina, every hit builds mana, Defend is on the left page. It locks the input to exactly the button she's talking about, which is slow for a returning player but really clean for a new one. The game gave me a reason to read every line.

Mark Something new this time that I did not notice before: Kailo and Hina have a different Combo here because they are fire and nature, not fire and light. It's called Pōhuehue, and instead of Simon it's a rhythm game, "Grow the vine!", notes with up, tab, up, tab, then z, timed to the beat. Five notes, I got five. 89 damage, and the boar fell. The Combo is different for every pair of stances, and each one is a different minigame. That is a great idea. I'd love to see how many there are.

Mark The ending is the same as before. "...yeah, bruised taro still cooks. I just hate seeing the rest go to waste." The Great Boar, "too fat to come get it himself", Hina saying "That is not how boars work." and Kailo going to "tell him to get his own taro." Hina: "I'll be at home. When you figure out you can't do this alone, you know where I live." And I stand where I was an hour ago, on the beach by the taro patch, with nothing.

Mark Hina joined again, same lines: "Did you forget what you were doing? You're hopeless, aren't you? Well, you need a healer anyway, so I'm coming too." And I like the new pop-up even more the second time: "While she is in your party, the fallen get back up after a win." Fine, and this time I'll treat that as a promise to test, not something to take on trust.

Mark Back in the forest with the lake. Two more roosters and a boar. A chest on the shore held one more Noni Pulu. The Papanok is the real danger in this area: it shifts between fire and light every turn, hastes itself so it acts two or three times, and its Sun Slash hit Hina for 47 and then 46, both "Weak!" She was down to 26 of 160. Kailo can hand items to her from his battle Bag: "Kailo gives Hina the Noni Pulu", +30. That's what I should have been doing against the troll, and something I only now noticed, because the Item command stayed grayed out until the game put a Noni Pulu x3 in his bag on its own.

Mark Right, so the bag is a tool, not a punishment. And the stance matters for survival more than for damage. Hina's light stance is weak to Sun Slash, which makes sense, a sun move against a sun priestess. I think the rooster picks whichever stance beats mine. If that's right, I should switch Hina to nature when roosters show up. I'll test it next fight.

Mark Quick aside before the second half. I left a few things out of the first half, and since I'm writing as I go I'll put them here instead of pretending I said them at the time.

Mark That's the field menu with Hina at full health, both of us in the stances I'd left them in. Still no Save line. I counted on it being there this time and it wasn't.

Mark And that's the "???" meal. "Makes whoever eats it sick." I like that the game keeps my failed banana soup in the bag as a souvenir.

Mark The area map, with a yellow dot on the harbor. The explored part is a small strip at the bottom and everything above it is black. The map only fills in where you've been, which I like, but it also shows how little of this island I've actually seen after two and a half hours.

Mark The taro patch from the beginning of the episode, with Melia's friend the grocer in the corner and the big hale on the right. You pick the taro and Hina tells you to replant, and "It takes a while to grow." I'd call that the best little teaching moment in the village.

Mark The forest sign and two boars with exclamation marks over their heads. Those marks are the game's way of saying "you've been noticed" and I like them a lot, they work in half a second.

Mark The grayed-out Combo, Tinju Surya, with fire and sun beside the name. It took me until the second half to understand why it was gray.

Mark Kailo's command page: Attack, Cook, Element, Item. Hina's is Attack, Scold, Element, Item. Same four slots, different job. Cook for Kailo, Scold for Hina. It's neat that a character's identity is a menu line.

Mark The orchard maze, with three boars already sniffing around. I never found the way in from the south.

Mark Same room, after I'd beaten the boar by the entrance. The bushes make a spiral and I walked up and down it for a good while.

Mark Here I am in a pocket in the middle of it, bush wall above me and a palm to the right. This is where I decided the maze was not for today.

Mark And here I'm at the east end, next to a banana palm. One more step east of this and the bridge appears. I only found it because I was trying to walk out of the room.

Mark The banyan island. Five Papanoks, two of them already marked, two sea monsters in the water, and a sandy road going north. I like how this room looks, with the pale trees against the water.

Mark The long boardwalk with Nuno sa Tulay standing in the middle of it and chests on three islets I can't reach. This is the picture I remember when I think about the toll.

Mark Left page of the commands, with Equip, Defend and a grayed Escape. In a boss fight Escape is gray and nothing says why. A short line like "You can't run from this one" would have saved me a minute at 6 HP.

Mark A tutorial moment from the second time through. Hina's mid-attack, the stamina bar is almost empty, and "Dodge" floats over a boar. That's how often my first Strong gets dodged, so I always keep a little stamina for a Light.

Mark The lake room again, with a rooster beside the chest and another one further down. I'm standing under a banyan I can't walk past.

Mark Okay, back to the real time. 31 minutes in I was standing on the taro beach with nothing, and the first thing I had to decide was whether to redo the intro, or to hurry through it. I hurried. I know Hina's lines by heart now, so I skipped the lessons I could and still got every one that the game forced on me: Hina locks the buttons, she only lets you press the one she's talking about. It's slow for me and wonderful for a new player.

Mark There's the first thing I'll call out as new: "The faces on the right are who goes next. The top one goes now." It's a short line and it's the thing the whole system depends on. I like that she says it first.

Mark And the parry lesson: "Here they come. Each red bar is one of the pig's hits." The meter is a black box with a yellow zone and three lanes. When the narrator told me the timing I could get all of them, but I feel for anyone who has to do it by eye.

Mark Hina's command page again, Attack, Scold, Element, Item. After I used Defend she kept getting turns three in a row, which tells me her actions cost almost nothing in the queue. It makes her a support character in a really mechanical way.

Mark Hina's house. A bed, a rug, a barrel of fish and greens and crabs, and Hina in the corner packing. "For my trip. I leave soon, and it's none of your business." I like that you can see she's packed: a bundle on the floor.

Mark The forest with the lake is the room I fought the most in. A boar gave me Thorn Strike, a rooster dropped Noni Pulu, then another dropped an Egg.

Mark The lake room as I walked in. Chests at the top left and right, a red mushroom, a water monster in the lake, a pond at the bottom right with a wooden post. That post is a Lanu offering place. I have two Fresh Water now, so I could offer one, but it gave nothing visible last time and I didn't want to spend the clock.

Mark Right side of the room after the rooster fight. The chest by the banyan only had a Noni Pulu in it.

Mark Then the Papanok hit Hina twice, "47" and "46", both marked "Weak!". She dropped to 26 of 160 in one turn. That's the closest I came to losing her, and I found out why afterwards: she was in her nature stance, which is weak to fire, and the rooster was in its fire stance. In the first half I'd had her in light, which resists fire. So her stance matters more than I had understood.

Mark Kailo's Item command has Noni Pulu x3 in it. I did not put them there; the game seems to have filled his Bag. "Kailo gives Hina the Noni Pulu." That's +30. It was the answer to the troll fight and I'd been walking around with the bag empty. That's a weakness in teaching: nothing told me to stock the bags.

Mark The Info menu. Quests, Bestiary, Glossary, Lore, Records. Time 0:14, Steps 58, "30th of Kau". Only one quest is on the list, "The Great Boar". This time the menu is at least easy to find.

Mark The quest entry: "Melia told you the Great Boar is the king of the boars in the woods. He has to be beaten before the woods are safe again." It tells me nothing about where to go. I understand wanting a mystery, but a single compass line would help.

Mark The map after about 40 minutes. Still just the village strip and the forest room. I've been through six rooms and two bridges, and none of this has a save point.

Mark The taro patch again. Two taro are lying on the ground, dug up by the boars, and I can pick them up. This is a good detail. It says the damage the boars did is real, not a cutscene.

Mark The farm terraces. Taro, wheat, and a Lanu post and pond in the top left corner. This time I'm not here for the post, I'm here because the bridge wants 100 pule and I have none. I decided the farm is the answer: picking a ripe plot gives two Taro, Taro sells for 4 and Wheat for 4.

Mark My ingredients: Taro x9, Fresh Water x2, Egg, Wheat x2. The description of Taro: "Recovers 5 HP. Lasts 14 days at sea." That's a very dry, very fun line. "At sea" tells me the Meialana's voyage is not far off.

Mark A view of the farm terraces from the east edge. Right now I'm planning a route through every ripe plot.

Mark Left terrace, middle row. I've harvested most of the ripe ones. The sprouts in the brown plots mean I planted them, or left them bare.

Mark Back at the grocer's.

Mark The grocer's buy list: Breadfruit 25, Flour 15, Noodles 30, Pia 15, Pineapple 25, Salt 5, and seeds. "Recovers 10 HP." Nothing here I need.

Mark "E komo mai! What'll it be?" Buy, Sell, Exit. That's "welcome" in Hawaiian. And it's a horizontal bar, not a list, so I tried down first and it did nothing.

Mark The sell list: Egg 5, Taro x17 at 4, Wheat x4 at 4. I sold everything: 89 pule. Short by eleven. Then I picked the last five taro from the village patch and sold those, 109. I'll say this plainly: it's the first time the game has shown me a way to make money without fighting, and it only exists if you wander into the farm.

Mark The village patch with two ripe taro left, and the boy standing next to the hale.

Mark On the way to the bridge I won three more fights. In one I switched Hina out of nature and into light, "Hina shifts into Shakan Mudras", because roosters were about. That worked: she took 10 and 18 instead of 47.

Mark Hina's Element list: Māla Hula, which is a stance, and Heal in gray. The stance sits at the top of the same list as the spells. That's elegant, and unexplained.

Mark And Hina said something during the fight, "Wait. We both have full mana, and we're side by side on the bar." then "That means a Combo. Press right on your commands." and "It takes every drop of mana we have. Don't mess up your half." So the game does teach Combos, but only when you're standing in the exact condition. I did not see it in the first half because I never hit that condition in a fight with Hina in a lesson mood. That answers my complaint from before, partly. I'd still like a line when the Combo is grayed out.

Mark The Combo itself is Simon again, then the punch, this time 212 on a Papanok with the circle at 17%. It's a lot of damage, yet the result is the same: a Combo ends a fight.

Mark At the toll I paid. "Kailo paid 100 pule." "Hehe. Now cross, quickly." And when I talked to him again he asked "Fight the Nuno sa Tulay?" with No highlighted. That's a nice rematch hook, and I said No. I'm not done with him, but I'm not walking back into that fight at half HP.

Mark Past the bridge, a boardwalk maze, five chests, four straw-hatted wanderers, and a beach at the north end with green and blue birds along it. This is the new area.

Mark The wanderers are Nuno sa Punso, the small cousins of the toll troll, and one of them fought me on the boards. A Weak! lightning, a ward of light, and then I won, and it dropped 'Awa Root, a Smoke Bomb and, for the first time, 17 pule. So that's where money comes from: some monsters drop it. I'd been looking for it for three episodes and it was behind a toll.

Mark Two chests so far on the planks, a Ti Leaf and another Noni Pulu. The three others I haven't reached.

Mark One correction to my own captions: the two pictures near the toll are the wrong way round. The one with the "Fight the Nuno sa Tulay?" box is the one I paired with the boardwalk maze, and the maze picture went with the Nuno sa Punso fight. Anyway, you can see both.

Mark The last few minutes. A second Nuno sa Punso and the birds came down the boardwalk toward me, and I won again with the Combo, 214 this time, the circle at 17%. It dropped a Kukui, the burn cure from Hoku's lesson, and my pule is up to 122. Hina is at 49 of 130, so I'm not going to walk into the birds.

Mark There they are coming down the middle bridge, a blue one and a green one, with a Nuno right under me on the planks.

Mark And this is where I stop. 60 minutes. Kailo is standing in the middle of the boardwalk maze, four wanderers and four birds still between me and the beach at the north end, three chests I haven't opened, 122 pule and no save point. I didn't find a save point again, so if I get thrown out of the game now it's the title screen. I'll say it plainly: that Game Over cost me about 20 minutes this hour and I never saw it coming.

Mark Thanks for watching, everybody. Good place to stop. Next time I want to open the other chests on these boards, learn what the birds are, find out what's at the north end of this beach, and still look for a save point and the hunters' lodge. And I'd like to go back to the bridge troll with a full bag and see if the second time is different.

End of episode

What happened

- Started on the harbor dock, 0 pule, no saves. Checked the field menu (no Save line). Walked to the grocer's taro patch, picked 2 plots (4 Taro), replanted both at Hina's prompting.

- North of the grocer into Kulāiwi Forest. Fight 1: two Pua'a Hihiu, won (Noni Pulu, Boar Hide, Seer's Shell). Fight 2: one boar in the orchard, won (Flambé). Fight 3: one boar, won (Boar Hide). Fight 4: ambush, one boar, won with a Tinju Surya Combo for 198 (Taro). Orchard maze: I could not find a way through to the north gap. East bridge to the banyan island. Fight 5: one Papanok, won (Red Feather). Fight 6: two Papanok, won (Egg, Flambé, Seer's Shell). Kailo went from 140 to 150 max HP.

- Boardwalk north of the banyan island. Nuno sa Tulay asked 100 pule. Chose "I'm not paying that." Boss fight, Kailo at 96 of 150. He shifted to spirit stance, cast a cyclone (Weak! against Kailo fire and Hina light), chain lightning, and acted two or three times in a row. My Combo did 95, "Resisted". Kailo's Cook was grayed out because Taro was not in his bag, Escape was grayed. Hina fell, then Kailo. Game Over, back to the title screen, Continue grayed out. 19:14 on the clock. Nothing was saved, so the game started over from the opening cards.

- New Game: the full opening, the taro patch tutorial against two Pua'a Hihiu with every lesson (queue, stamina, mana, Sauté, Defend, parry, Hina's Heal), a Pōhuehue Combo (rhythm game) that finished the second boar (89). Then the same cutscene: the stew ruined, the Great Boar, Hina's "I'll be at home." Reached Hina's house at about 32 minutes, she joined.

- Forest with the lake: a boar (Thorn Strike), a Papanok (Noni Pulu), another Papanok (Egg), chest on the shore (Noni Pulu, the second chest at the same spot was already empty). The north gap of that room was walled off by banyans, I could not get to it. Hina dropped to 26 of 160 to a Papanok's weak hits; Kailo gave her a Noni Pulu from his battle Bag (+30).

- Info menu: one quest, "The Great Boar". Walked east through the Chief's room to the farm terraces. Harvested ripe plots (2 Taro each), planted one, picked wheat. Went back to the grocer: sold Egg 5, Taro 4, Wheat 4. 89 pule, then 5 more Taro from the village patch: 109 pule. One more boar fight on the way (Boar Hide, Seed of Endurance).

- Banyan island, two Papanok (Hina switched to light stance, won with a Tinju Surya Combo, 212; dropped Red Feather x2, Seed of Perception). Paid the toll (109 to 9 pule). Nuno sa Tulay asked "Fight the Nuno sa Tulay?" if talked to again; said No. Past the bridge: a boardwalk maze with five chests, four wandering Nuno sa Punso, and a north beach with four birds. Fight 1 vs a Nuno sa Punso: won ('Awa Root, Smoke Bomb, 17 pule). Opened two chests (Ti Leaf, Noni Pulu). Fight 2 vs a Nuno sa Punso: won with a Tinju Surya Combo (214; Kukui, 13 pule).

- Ended at 60:06 on the boardwalk, 122 pule, Kailo 97 of 130, Hina 49 of 130, not saved, birds approaching.

Stuck and confusing

1. Game Over with no warning. The party fell in the Nuno sa Tulay fight. The narrator said "The party has fallen." then "Screen: game over", then "Screen: title", "Highlighted: New Game", Continue grayed. I pressed z. Nothing had been saved because I could not find a save point, so the whole game restarted. The choice that caused it ("I'm not paying that. This bridge is free for everyone to use.") did not say it starts a boss fight.

2. Boss fights: Escape is grayed out with no explanation. On the left page I saw Equip, Defend and a grayed Escape.

3. Combo grayed out with no reason. Tinju Surya sat grayed out in Kailo's Combo menu when Kailo and Hina were not both at 7 of 7 mana, and also when they were not next to each other on the turn bar. The narrator only said "Highlighted: Tinju Surya (grayed out)". The only explanation I saw came from Hina in the second run when both were full: "Wait. We both have full mana, and we're side by side on the bar."

4. Cook grayed out in the boss fight. "Highlighted: Poi (grayed out)", because Taro was in my pack, not in Kailo's battle Bag. Nothing told me the battle Bag matters. The Item command was grayed out too until the game put Noni Pulu x3 in Kailo's Bag by itself in the second half.

5. The orchard maze. I pressed up in several columns and got "toward something solid" every time. The north gap was "5 up" and I never found the path. The same with the lake room's north gap.

6. The Combo minigames are not explained. The narrator tells you the keys for the lights game, but the game never says what the punch's circle is for. I found it by pressing z at about 0.9 seconds.

7. Walk commands on the boardwalk: several times I walked "right 8" or "up 5" and ended up in a different place than the narrator led me to expect, because planks that look connected are not. The left plank with the chest is a dead end.

8. The shop menu is a horizontal bar. I pressed down first and nothing happened. The narrator said "Shop: Buy, Sell, Exit; highlighted: Buy".

9. Two of my screenshot captions are swapped (near the toll): the picture with the "Fight the Nuno sa Tulay?" box and the picture of the boardwalk maze.

Design notes

1. A Game Over that wipes the game when there is no save point is the biggest problem. Reason: it costs the player everything they did and the only way to avoid it is to find a save point, which I could not find in more than three hours across three episodes. Large.

2. The Nuno sa Tulay toll is a good idea with bad information. The three answers (pay, fight, go around) are a real choice, but the game does not say that "fight" is a boss, and the boss has a cyclone that is "Weak!" against both starting stances. Reason: the player picks a fight with a boss without being told. Large.

3. The Combo is the best thing in the game. Reason: every pair of stances has its own minigame (Simon plus a shrinking punch for fire and light, a rhythm "Grow the vine!" for fire and nature), the payoff is large (198, 212, 214, 89), and the queue adjacency and full-mana rule makes you plan. Praise. Large.

4. The Combo condition is not explained at the menu. Reason: Combo shows "grayed out" for two different reasons (mana, adjacency) and a third (the partner is not next). Hina explains it once, in the middle of a fight, when it is first true. A line on the grayed entry would fix it. Medium.

5. Stance as an armour type is deep and well hidden. Reason: Papanok's Sun Slash did 47 and 46 to Hina in nature stance, and 10 to 18 in light. Weak shows only after you are hit. A visible stance weakness on the enemy or a short line in the log would help. Medium.

6. The battle Bag works, and is also invisible. Reason: "Kailo gives Hina the Noni Pulu" at +30 saved Hina, but the Bag starts empty and the game does not point at it. Medium.

7. The farm economy is a good discovery. Reason: planting and harvesting Taro, selling at 4 each, is a real loop, and Hina teaches the replant. But I had to find out by walking into the farm. The Info menu has no "ways to make pule". Small to medium.

8. Pule drops from monsters, not from the early ones. Reason: the boars and roosters gave none; the first money came from Nuno sa Punso on the far side of the toll, 17 and 13 pule. That means the toll itself has to be paid by farming. Medium.

9. Tutorial lock-in is clean. Reason: Hina locks the keys to what she says, so a new player cannot get lost, but it costs about ten minutes on a repeat. Small. A "skip lessons" choice did exist at the start but I could not tell I had taken it.

10. The parry meter's timing information is clear through the narrator, but a string of identical blows (seven Light) is easier than a mixed one, and two blows 0.1 seconds apart are very hard. Reason: the rule is "one press per blow at its own time". Small.

11. The writing is the strongest thing. Reason: Hina's "Then stop shouting and do something about it", "You're hopeless, aren't you?", the Nuno's "No? NO? Then I'll take it out of your hide!" and the Taro description "Lasts 14 days at sea". Praise. Medium.

12. The world detail is good. Reason: taro lying on the ground where the boars dug, a map that only fills in where you have been, folk names (Nuno sa Tulay, Nuno sa Punso) used as monsters. Praise. Small.

13. Level geometry: trees and bushes wall off two north exits (orchard maze and the lake room's north gap) with no hint. Reason: the player cannot tell whether a path exists. Medium.

14. Hina's heal-after-a-win promise was not tested, because I never won a fight with someone down. The first run ended in a loss and the second I kept both alive. Open.

Story and characters

- The opening is the same: a cook, a priestess, the last day of summer, the wake for Old Pono, boars in the taro patch, the Great Boar who sends the little ones to steal taro. Hina does not believe the Great Boar story ("That is not how boars work.") and Kailo is going anyway.

- Kailo: a cook, warm, a little proud, stands his ground. In the troll scene I picked "I'm not paying that" because he would, and it lost him the game.

- Hina: sharp and caring, packing for a trip she won't explain ("For my trip. I leave soon, and it's none of your business."), comes along because Kailo needs a healer. Teaches in a dry voice. She makes the tutorial work.

- Melia: Kailo's little sister (the quest gives her name as the quest giver), wants to fight with her sling.

- Noelani, Chief Ulu, the Loremaster, Nene and the rest I did not talk to this episode.

- Nuno sa Tulay: a toll troll from a Filipino folk figure, short-tempered, vain, offers a rematch. Nuno sa Punso are his smaller cousins that wander the boards.

- New place: a boardwalk maze beyond the bridge, with four birds (blue and green) at the north beach. I do not know what they are.

- The taro description "Lasts 14 days at sea" suggests the trip off the island is not far away.

Predictions

- Old, open: Hina is the devout priestess from the card (right: the Teacher said so in Episode 2). Somebody in the south takes mana from beaten champions (open). Poi for Nene and the stew will matter at the wake (open). Noelani's 'awapuhi is Pono's ginger (open). The Great Boar is in the Lost Woods (open; this episode's quest text says "the woods"). Hina's loyalty is split (open). The stances are gods' gifts (open). Five Lanu posts (open). Kailo's father a Kame Kingdom fighter (open). Thorn Strike is Hina's (open; I got two this episode but did not test who can use it). The Great Boar opens a third Element slot (open). The Meialana carries the party off Māla Iki after the wake (open; the Taro line "Lasts 14 days at sea" supports it). Chests across water open once the party can fight in water (open; I saw five on the boardwalk and more on islets). Noelani is Kailo and Melia's mother (open).

- Right: boars in nature stance are weak to fire (Sauté did 24 and 25 with "Weak!"). Hina in nature is weak to fire (Papanok in fire stance hit her for 47 and 46, "Weak!"); in light she took 10 and 18. Melia is Kailo's younger sister (the quest page says Melia). A Combo ends a fight (198, 212, 214).

- Wrong: "No save point means every risk is too costly" was not wrong, it was proven right by the Game Over. My plan to beat Nuno sa Tulay at 96 of 150 was wrong.

- New, open: the money loop is Taro and drops from monsters beyond the toll. The birds at the north beach are the next fight and their stance may be wind or spirit. The Nuno sa Tulay's cyclone is Weak! against fire and light, so water or nature might resist it. Hina's heal-after-a-win promise will be tested the first time one of us falls and we win. The hunters' lodge is north of the boardwalk. A save point will turn up on the far side of the toll.

The booklet

Never opened. I was confused about the Combo gray-out and about how the bags work, but I worked both out from the screen, and I was not stuck.

Review so far

Nuitai is trying to be a Chrono Cross style RPG with Tales-style timing, set in a Polynesian and Southeast Asian ocean world, and it does a few things better than the games it borrows from. The turn bar with real time costs, the Combo that needs two characters at full mana side by side, and the stance that changes your HP and what you are weak to are all good, and the Combo minigames, with the payoff of 200 damage, are the best thing I have seen here. The writing is the other strong point: Hina and the Nuno are very good, and small details like taro left on the ground make the village feel lived in.

What does not work is the safety net. There is no save point I could find in three hours, a boss that looks like a toll gate, a grayed Escape, a grayed Combo and a grayed Cook that never say why, and a Bag that has to be stocked by the player and is never mentioned. I lost twenty minutes to a Game Over that wiped the whole game. I'd recommend it today to patient people who like to find systems out for themselves, not yet to most, and I'd give it to anyone once it has a save point and a boss warning.

My notes for next time

- State at the end: standing on the boardwalk maze beyond the toll bridge, Kailo 97 of 130 (fire stance), Hina 49 of 130 (light stance, switched from nature), 122 pule, not saved. Bag has Noni Pulu, Boar Hide x3+, Red Feather, Egg and so on. The first game is gone. Hina joined again.

- People and places: Hina's house is the first door west of the start room's centre. Hina packing: "For my trip. I leave soon, and it's none of your business." Melia's quest: the Great Boar is the king of the boars in the woods. The grocer is in the taro patch room, welcome is "E komo mai!". Sell: Egg 5, Taro 4, Wheat 4. Buy: Breadfruit 25 (+10 HP), Flour 15, Noodles 30, Pia 15, Pineapple 25, Salt 5, Taro Seed 10, Wheat Seed 10, 'Uala Seed 25, Akai Seed 25. The taro patch in the grocer room can be picked and replanted. The farm terraces: east of the Chief's room, up a lane. Taro 4 pule each.

- The route north: grocer room north gap, forest room, orchard (maze: bridge is on the east side at the end of the row I walked from the entrance, up 4 then right), banyan island with Papanoks, the long bridge north, Nuno sa Tulay toll 100 pule, then the boardwalk maze with five chests (two opened: Ti Leaf, Noni Pulu) and a north beach with four birds. Nuno sa Punso wanderers drop pule (17, 13).

- Rules: the turn bar, Attack strokes Light 1, Medium 2, Strong 3 of 7 stamina. Combo needs both at 7 of 7 and side by side. Fire and light is Tinju Surya (lights game, then punch: wait about 0.97s, circle 17%, about 200 damage); fire and nature is Pōhuehue (rhythm: up, tab, up, tab, up, tab, z; 89). Stance affects weakness: Hina in nature is weak to fire (Papanok), light resists it. Papanok hastes itself and shifts fire and light. Nuno sa Tulay: spirit stance, cyclone Weak! for both stances, chain lightning, acts two or three times in a row, Combo is resisted (95). Kailo can give items to Hina from his Bag (Noni Pulu +30). Cook needs Taro in his Bag.

- Theories: save point is past the toll; hunters' lodge too; Boar Hide gets sold there; Great Boar is north; Lanu posts: two seen (pond and post in the lake room, pond and post in the farm).

- Next: open the other chests on the boards, fight or avoid the north beach birds, find a save point and the lodge, sell Boar Hide, put Taro and Noni Pulu in the bags before any boss, switch Hina to light stance before roosters, and see if the troll's rematch works with full bags.
